**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Pure Mathematics with Mechanics, Paper 3 (0765/3), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2022. Time allowed: three hours.**

Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. All questions carry equal marks. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. Start each question on a fresh page.
enonce_intro_markdown:
The position vector $\mathbf{r}$ of a particle of mass $3\ \mathrm{kg}$ at time $t$ seconds is given by

$$\mathbf{r} = [(3\sin 2t)\mathbf{i} + (4\cos 2t)\mathbf{j}]\ \mathrm{m}.$$

Find when $t = \dfrac{\pi}{8}$,
incertitudes: Le sujet n'imprime pas de total de points par question ; l'énoncé dit seulement « All questions carry equal marks ». Les points imprimés par partie somment à 13 pour chacune des 8 questions (total 104) ; `points` de l'exercice est laissé vide.

Question 1 (c) : « the power developed by the particle » est lu comme la puissance de la force agissant sur la particule, P = F.v (valeur confirmée par la dérivée de l'énergie cinétique). Le sujet n'imprime pas d'autre précision.

questions.enonce_markdown: the magnitude of the momentum of the particle,
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Set-up.** $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ are unit vectors along fixed perpendicular axes, $m = 3\ \mathrm{kg}$. The velocity is the derivative of the position vector with respect to time:

$$\mathbf{v} = \frac{d\mathbf{r}}{dt} = (6\cos 2t)\,\mathbf{i} - (8\sin 2t)\,\mathbf{j}\ \ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$$

At $t = \dfrac{\pi}{8}$ we have $2t = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$, so $\sin 2t = \cos 2t = \dfrac{\sqrt2}{2}$:

$$\mathbf{v} = 6\cdot\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\,\mathbf{i} - 8\cdot\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\,\mathbf{j} = (3\sqrt2\,\mathbf{i} - 4\sqrt2\,\mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$$

Speed: $|\mathbf{v}| = \sqrt{(3\sqrt2)^2 + (4\sqrt2)^2} = \sqrt{18 + 32} = \sqrt{50} = 5\sqrt2\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.

**Momentum** $\mathbf{p} = m\mathbf{v} = (9\sqrt2\,\mathbf{i} - 12\sqrt2\,\mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, so

$$|\mathbf{p}| = m|\mathbf{v}| = 3\times 5\sqrt2 = 15\sqrt2 \approx 21.2\ \mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$$

**Magnitude of the momentum $= 15\sqrt2 \approx 21.2\ \mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: the force acting on the particle,
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Acceleration.** Differentiate the velocity from part (a):

$$\mathbf{a} = \frac{d\mathbf{v}}{dt} = (-12\sin 2t)\,\mathbf{i} - (16\cos 2t)\,\mathbf{j}\ \ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$$

At $t = \dfrac{\pi}{8}$ (where $\sin 2t = \cos 2t = \dfrac{\sqrt2}{2}$):

$$\mathbf{a} = (-6\sqrt2\,\mathbf{i} - 8\sqrt2\,\mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$$

**Newton's second law** (constant mass): $\mathbf{F} = m\mathbf{a} = 3\mathbf{a}$, so

$$\mathbf{F} = (-18\sqrt2\,\mathbf{i} - 24\sqrt2\,\mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{N},\qquad |\mathbf{F}| = \sqrt{(18\sqrt2)^2 + (24\sqrt2)^2} = \sqrt{648 + 1152} = 30\sqrt2 \approx 42.4\ \mathrm{N}$$

(Remark: $\mathbf{a} = -4\mathbf{r}$ for every $t$, so the force always points towards the origin, $\mathbf{F} = -12\,\mathbf{r}$; at $t=\pi/8$, $|\mathbf{r}| = \sqrt{(3\sqrt2/2)^2 + (2\sqrt2)^2} = \sqrt{12.5}$ and $12\sqrt{12.5} = 30\sqrt2$, which confirms the result.)

**Force $\mathbf{F} = (-18\sqrt2\,\mathbf{i} - 24\sqrt2\,\mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{N}$, of magnitude $30\sqrt2 \approx 42.4\ \mathrm{N}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: the power developed by the particle.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The power developed is the rate at which the force acting on the particle does work: $P = \mathbf{F}\cdot\mathbf{v}$.

With $\mathbf{F} = (-18\sqrt2,\,-24\sqrt2)$ and $\mathbf{v} = (3\sqrt2,\,-4\sqrt2)$ from parts (a) and (b):

$$P = (-18\sqrt2)(3\sqrt2) + (-24\sqrt2)(-4\sqrt2) = -108 + 192 = 84\ \mathrm{W}$$

**Check with kinetic energy.** $v^2 = 36\cos^2 2t + 64\sin^2 2t = 36 + 28\sin^2 2t$, so $E_k = \tfrac12 m v^2 = \tfrac32(36 + 28\sin^2 2t)$ and

$$\frac{dE_k}{dt} = \tfrac32\cdot 28\cdot 2\sin 2t\cos 2t\cdot 2 = 84\sin 4t$$

At $t = \pi/8$, $\sin 4t = \sin(\pi/2) = 1$, giving $84\ \mathrm{W}$ again.

**Power $= 84\ \mathrm{W}$** (positive: the particle is gaining kinetic energy at this instant).
